notes.title: Rail Network
notes.notes:
>“It is said that if all the routes were measured for the total length of this railway network, it could wrap around our world up to 100 times.”

No one knows when this railway network was built or who built it. All that is known is that every route within the network is amazingly interconnected, and there are a vast number of routes.
At present, the railway network remains largely unexplored, and its durability and strength remain a mystery—despite the lack of maintenance and the fact that the tracks have never been destroyed. This is according to historical records following the fall of humanity.

notes.title: Random Event
notes.notes:
Unexpected events often occur during the journey. On some days, you might find your train caught in a sandstorm. On others, your train could be ambushed by Soksai or attacked by bandits along the way. If you're lucky, you may even gain a new crew member to help on board.

Therefore, you must always be prepared for whatever may come. Stock up on food, weapons, and medicine—be ready!!

notes.title: Soksai sighting report#2 (Imature Soksai)
notes.notes:
Soksai sighting report#2 Imature Soksai

A Small Soksai. They often gather together in large swarm. The average body size is 45-55 cm. It has a segmented body and hard wings to protect itself from sandstorms so that It can fly against the sandstorm. This type of Soksai has an antenna to communicate with another Soksai. However, When it’s alone, it’s weak. Therefore, If it want to attack an enemy, it will attack with its swarm.

notes.title: Soksai sighting report#1 (Tank Soksai)
notes.notes:
Soksai sighting report#1 Tank Soksai
Soksai with Armored.  It is the most common Soksai. They evolve from Imature Soksai that absorb enough nutrients to evolve wings into a strong shell. The average height is 2-2.5 meters and has heavyweight. This type of Soksai is often an opening when attacking something because it has enough endurance to withstand attacks. Tank Soksai usually attacks by using its body to smash the target. However, the movement is quite slow when compared to other types of Soksai.

notes.title: Carriage And Room Explain
notes.notes:
In The Post-Apocalypse World, The Survivor create trains for travel and contact between cities. Traveling somewhere takes days, months, and even years. The interior of the train is divided into various rooms so that the crew can survive. So Many Travelers rely on trains as a Home.

The rooms inside the train are divided into different room types according to their use, such as Crafting rooms, Cultivate rooms, Living rooms, Storage rooms, and Engine rooms.

Carriages come in many sizes. From small to large, some carriage has their own functions, such as Dustcollector Carriage for product material or Container vans for carrying various items, Coal carts for transporting charcoal, engines for speed boost, etc.

notes.title: Soksai
notes.notes:
[i]“Their hive has been destroyed countless times over the years, yet it seems the battle will never end”[/i]

Soksai is one of the most common enemies in the Lost Heaven Station world.
They emerged alongside the collapse of human civilization. Though no one truly understands what they are or where they came from, one thing is certain—they are relentless in their attack on humanity.

Soksai resembles massive insect-like creatures, They operate in swarms, much like a hive. They have various types and roles, each essential to fulfill their hive, and all are driven by an overwhelming instinct to hunt and destroy, making them a relentless threat wherever they appear.

notes.title: Why Lost Heaven?
notes.notes:
[i]"....Beyond the endless rails lies Lost Heaven, a sanctuary of the mighty God.”[/i]
[b]Why do we have to look for Lost Heaven?
[/b]
Lost Heaven Station is the ultimate goal for travelers and survivors in this post-apocalyptic world. Whether driven by belief, hope, or the simple need to survive, many believe Lost Heaven Station exists. Though proof is hard to find, people believe in its reality. The most common clues include a mysterious radio that plays old songs and some documents scattered around different places.

Most people believe that the Lost Heaven Station is a safe haven where parts of the old world still survive. It’s thought to be a place where one can live without having to go outside. People also believe it has special technology that can protect them completely from the dangerous Soksai, making it a true sanctuary.

notes.title: What is Lost Heaven Station
notes.notes:
[b]In Post-apocalypse world you need everything to survive[/b]

[b]Lost Heaven Station[/b] is Strategy Colony-Sim Management for players to create a base in their own train and travel around the world to find a ‘Lost Heaven’

The game focuses on a [b]Colony-Sim[/b] experience, where players must manage their crew aboard a train, ensuring their survival in a [b]Post-apocalypse[/b] world.

The core gameplay revolves around expanding and upgrading the train to meet the crew’s growing needs. Players will cultivate resources, such as mushrooms for sustenance, craft essential items, explore new route, and equip their crew with weapons to defend against the constant threats encountered throughout their journey.

notes.title: devlog 1.7.0
notes.notes:
**BU Game On! Lost Heaven Station 2024!**

For the past 2nd of December 2024, *Lost Heaven Station* was selected for the BU Game On! Award, and we are proud to announce that we have won the Jury Choices Award, along with a prize of 6,000 Baht. We would like to extend our sincere thanks to all the visitors and supporters who made our time at the BU Game On! exhibition such a rewarding experience. Your support and encouragement have been invaluable to us!

=====================================================

Steam Page: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3227980/Lost_Heaven_Station/

=====================================================

As we plan for version 1.7, the main goal is to focus on the station and the life of the crew, creating a more complete picture of the game. Before we dive into the station itself, we aim to introduce parallel elements that will enhance the gameplay, making it more dynamic and adventurous. In this patch (1.7.0), we prioritized developing these parallel elements as part of the main goal.

# **Update Summary 1.7.0H**

**Note:** The parallel system still has some issues, which need to be complete the station first.

### Parallel System: New Transitions and Backgrounds

- **New:** Added parallel backgrounds.
- Transition tunnels now enable transitions between backgrounds.
- Each route can now have a unique parallel background.
- Transition tunnels scale based on the length of the player's carriage.
- The transition tunnel now automatically calculates the optimal starting point for transitions.

### **Event & Route**

- Added new events and concept art
- Introduced a new location.
- Rebalanced route and event.
- The ‘Fading Signal’ event is now recommended to be found at near end of normal route it’s lead to the ‘Lost Heaven’ route for end-game progression.

### **Spawn point**

- Spawn points have been updated to hook to each train.
- Groups can now spawn at the same spawn point.

### **Crew**

- Added new shooting animation.
- Combat calculations now include accuracy, miss, evade, damage, and attack speed.

### **Storage**

- Storage now allows toggling to specify which resources should be stored.
- Resource restrictions can now be set for storage.
- balance storage space

## **Optimization & Bug Fixes**

### **UI panel**

- Improved Room Detail panel to show negative debuffs.
- Enhanced alert UI icon on the top-left panel.
- Added a way to access the Carriage Set panel.
- Left button functionality improved for opening and closing panels.

### **Other**

- Storage functionality fixed.
- Event reader bug fixed.
- Spawn point bug fixed.
- Fixed work positions for cleaning/maintenance tasks.
- Fixed day/night cycle lighting timing.
- Fixed Priority Panel display.
- Fixed issue allowing movement of the train despite being overweight.
- Item detail display bug fixed.

notes.title: devlog 1.6.12 : Tutorial Is Main Experience
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello, it’s been a while![/h1]

After some our review, we've decided to update our devlogs every 2-4 weeks, depending on the readiness. We recommend following along with each major update for the best overview.

In next version 1.7, our main goal is to introduce basic planning features, like life and station systems, to start building a complete picture of the game. By incorporating all core mechanics, we’ll have a solid foundation, allowing us to refine each feature in the future for the best quality and management.

Thanks for your patience!

[h1]Update Summary 1.6.12[/h1]
**Note:** The crew doctor role is still in testing

[h3]Tutorial[/h3]
- Major rework of the tutorial
- For now on, using tutorial steps to guide the main gameplay experience—we recommend starting with the tutorial

[h3]Creatures Behavior[/h3]
- **New:** Creatures (crew and enemies) now have states for downed or dead
- **New:** Crew can now tend to downed crew members (doctor role)
- **New:** Crew members can carry injured crew to a safe location

[h3]Event & Route[/h3]
- Added new events and concept art
- Events and locations can now be fixed within routes
- Rebalanced event dynamics

[h3]Sound[/h3]
- Changed the main background OST

[h2]Optimization & Bug Fixes[/h2]

[h3]UI panel[/h3]
- Improved order UI and build mode experience
- Optimized crafting order functionality
- Added animations for panel opening

[h3]Other[/h3]
- Improved crew force controls
- Fixed issues with selecting crew within selection boxes
- Resolved bugs when switching from sleep to explore
- Fixed event reading/running display
- Fixed abandon carriage errors
- Synchronized animations frames
- Smoother camera movement
- Results now display when adding resources during events or after exploration
- Added ability to pause building construction if not ready to complete
